doc.title: Ada Rovatti interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 13, 2022

title: Gaps in her training and honest practice
summary: She still feels her time and basics are shaky and works on finding what is not working.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Well it’s interesting because Randy explained a bit in our interview about the way both of you work and some of the technology but when you said occasionally you run into things that you still are missing in your music education, can you be specific about that?

Just I swear it’s like simple stuff you know. I still feel that sometimes my time is wiggly woggly and just like sometimes my ideas they don’t — you know they are simple things that probably for any beginner musician will be the first step that you do it. And I skipped some of the steps because maybe I was, technically I was a little more advanced so I was more going for the idea and then I realized yeah, but I slop it up all the way to the idea so I need to slow down, you know, the metronome hello — is there to be used not as a centerpiece of a table. So a lot of things. But also you know clearly more you study more, you play more, you advance the more you go looking for the little problem and that’s where you know the last few years has been — just find what’s not working, you know? Because I can enjoy, just flatter myself how can I sound good on that, but that’s not the point you know. In this room that’s where I want to see where I suck (sorry my French). You know that’s where I wanted to see where I messed up things and where I need to be really honest with myself where, you know, where I do the mistake. And I need to take care here. So that’s, you know, it’s hard to kind of look at yourself and see your flaw and acknowledge them and be willing to change them.
